advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile per-snapshot `_missing_sources_finding` with newest-only `snapshot_missing_sources` so the diagnostic and the rebuild refuse-gate agree when a ticket has multiple active snapshots.
evidence: compact_rebuild.py:56 `snaps = [n for n in names if is_active_event(n) and n.endswith("-SNAPSHOT.json")]` then line 60 opens only `snaps[-1]`
fsck.py:168-173 `_snap_findings` iterates `for snap_name in sorted(...)` and calls `_check_snapshot` for EACH, which at fsck.py:367 calls `_missing_sources_finding` per snapshot
The refuse gate `_refuse_incomplete_log` (compact_rebuild.py:80) and `_dry_run_plan_line` (fsck.py:332) both call `snapshot_missing_sources`, which only reads the newest snapshot
advisory.finding: `snapshot_missing_sources()` (the refuse-gate and dry-run source of truth) inspects ONLY the newest active snapshot (`snaps[-1]`), but `_missing_sources_finding()` is invoked per-snapshot from `_check_snapshot()` for every active SNAPSHOT file. When a ticket has more than one active snapshot, fsck can report `SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES` for a superseded snapshot while the rebuild refuse-gate / dry-run plan (keyed on the newest snapshot) disagree — so a ticket flagged as 'NOT auto-rebuildable' by the diagnostic could still be rebuilt (or shown 'would rebuild').

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the dry-run test to assert the specific 'DRY-RUN: would SKIP' classification for the missing-sources ticket, not just the 'DRY-RUN' substring.
evidence: assert "DRY-RUN" in res.stdout, "a dry run must print the per-ticket plan"
_dry_run_plan_line emits two distinct lines: `f"DRY-RUN: would SKIP {ticket_id} ..."` (fsck.py:335) vs `f"DRY-RUN: would rebuild SNAPSHOT for {ticket_id}"` (fsck.py:338)
The seeded ticket has missing sources (_legacy_compacted_closed_ticket cites deleted_close_uuid), so the correct line is 'would SKIP', but the assertion cannot distinguish it from the rebuild line.
advisory.finding: test_repair_snapshots_dry_run_writes_nothing asserts only the generic substring `'DRY-RUN' in res.stdout`; it does not assert the SKIP classification ('would SKIP ...' for the incomplete-log ticket it seeds). The test would still pass if the b636 fail-closed classification regressed and the dry run emitted 'would rebuild SNAPSHOT for' for a missing-sources ticket instead of 'would SKIP'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `"would SKIP" in res.stdout` (or the full SKIP line) so the SKIP-vs-rebuild classification is verified.

evidence: return f"DRY-RUN: would rebuild SNAPSHOT for {ticket_id}"  (fsck.py:338, no test asserts this line)
The only dry-run test (test_repair_snapshots_dry_run_writes_nothing) seeds _legacy_compacted_closed_ticket, whose snapshot cites a deleted source, forcing the SKIP branch.

No test constructs a complete-log ticket with a SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT/ORPHAN_EVENT/SNAPSHOT_STALE_CHANNEL finding and runs 'fsck --repair-snapshots --dry-run' to assert it prints 'would rebuild' AND leaves the store unmutated.
advisory.finding: The 'would rebuild SNAPSHOT for' branch of _dry_run_plan_line (a complete-log ticket carrying a rebuildable finding, previewed under --dry-run without mutation) is exercised by no test. Only the SKIP branch (incomplete log) is seeded. The primary positive path of the new --dry-run support — 'this ticket would be safely rebuilt, no bytes written' — is untested.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 592 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug b636-f31a-d590-4642 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan b636-f31a-d590-4642` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review b636-f31a-d590-4642` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan b636-f31a-d590-4642 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_dry_run_plan_line` account for the reduce-failure abort path so the plan matches what a live rebuild would actually do.
evidence: fsck.py:332-338 `_dry_run_plan_line` only calls `snapshot_missing_sources`; it returns 'would rebuild' otherwise
compact_rebuild.py:111-114 the live path additionally aborts when `reduce_ticket(...) is None or status in ('error','fsck_needed')`
dropped.finding: `_dry_run_plan_line` prints `DRY-RUN: would rebuild SNAPSHOT for {ticket_id}` whenever the ticket is 'rebuildable' and has no missing sources, but it does not re-run the reduce-validity check (`reduce_ticket(...).status in ('error','fsck_needed')`) that `_rebuild_source_state` applies at live-run time. A ticket that would actually be refused for a failed reduce is still previewed as 'would rebuild', so the dry-run plan can overstate what a live run will do.
